definition: modest; keeping oneself out of the spotlight
chinese: 謙遜低調的；不愛出風頭的
example: Despite her fame, the self-effacing scientist credited her students for nearly every discovery.

definition: acting to make oneself seem more important
chinese: 自我吹捧的；自我抬高的
example: His self-aggrandizing memoir exaggerated his role in events he had barely witnessed.

definition: shyness resulting from a lack of self-confidence
example: Her diffidence in seminars belied the boldness of her written arguments.
The committee's timidity allowed a minor problem to grow into a crisis.

definition: guided by ideals rather than practical concerns
chinese: 理想主義的；不切實際的
example: The idealistic reformers underestimated how entrenched the old bureaucracy was.

definition: the pursuit of high principles, often unrealistically
example: Youthful idealism gave way to a wary pragmatism after years in government.
The mayor's pragmatism won over voters weary of ideological battles.

chinese: 漫不經心；若無其事；冷淡
example: He received the alarming news with a nonchalance that unsettled his colleagues.
What critics called indolence was in fact a deliberate refusal to rush the work.

definition: tendency to remain unchanged; lack of motivation to act
example: Institutional inertia kept the outdated policy in place for decades.

chinese: 有進取心的；有創業精神的
example: An enterprising graduate student turned the abandoned lab into a thriving workshop.
The meticulousness of her footnotes left reviewers little to dispute.

definition: excessive concern about accuracy or cleanliness
example: His fastidiousness about wording delayed the report by weeks.

definition: strict attention to detail or correct behavior
example: The diplomat's punctiliousness about protocol was legendary.
The rehearsed speech lacked the spontaneity of her earlier remarks.

chinese: 即興創作；即興表演；臨時拼湊
example: The jazz trio's improvisation made each performance unique.

chinese: 經過深思熟慮的；慎重的
example: Her considered judgment carried more weight than his hasty objections.
The novelist mocks the naiveté of travelers who expect every village to be quaint.
Reviewers were skeptical of claims that the drug had no side effects.
Healthy skepticism kept the team from accepting the first plausible explanation.

chinese: 不加批判的；盲目接受的
example: The biography offers an uncritical portrait that ignores its subject's failures.

chinese: 欺騙性的；誤導的；虛有其表的
example: The apparent simplicity of the poem is deceptive.
The unprincipled lobbyist switched sides whenever it paid to do so.
Some biologists ask whether seemingly altruistic behavior in animals is truly selfless.

chinese: 自私自利的；只為自己打算的
example: The executive's apology seemed self-serving rather than sincere.

chinese: 冷酷無情的；麻木不仁的
example: The report's unfeeling tone angered the families it described.
In victory she showed a magnanimity her opponents had not expected.
The founder's frugality was evident in the company's spartan offices.
Generations of thrift allowed the family to survive the recession.
The junior researchers were deferential to the point of never questioning her methods.
The sycophantic aides told the minister only what he wished to hear.

definition: v. to give way or surrender; to produce; n. amount produced
chinese: v. 讓步；屈服；產生；n. 產量；收益
example: The negotiators refused to yield on any point of substance.
Few voters were disposed to trust a candidate who had changed positions so often.

definition: strong, often biased support for a party
example: Bitter partisanship stalled even uncontroversial legislation.
The historian's objectivity was questioned once her family ties became known.

definition: the quality of being brief and clear
example: The editor admired the concision of a writer who never used two words where one sufficed.

definition: too strong or subtle to be put into words
chinese: 無法言喻的；難以表達的
example: The poem tries to capture an inexpressible sense of loss.

definition: use of shocking content to provoke interest
example: The documentary avoided sensationalism, letting quiet testimony speak for itself.
The director's restraint makes the film's final scene all the more powerful.

definition: to represent as greater than is true
example: Early reports exaggerated the damage, causing needless panic.
It would be hard to overstate the influence of her early essays.

definition: excessive tendency to instruct or moralize
example: The novel's heavy didacticism alienated readers seeking entertainment.

definition: designed to be practical and useful; working
chinese: 實用的；功能性的；運作正常的
example: The architect favored functional design over decorative flourishes.
Fears that the vaccine caused infertility proved unfounded.
The senator dismissed the accusations as baseless.

definition: not shown to be right or reasonable
chinese: 不合理的；無正當理由的
example: Critics called the sudden price increase unjustified.

definition: based on guesswork rather than evidence
example: Any date for the manuscript remains conjectural until the paper is analyzed.

chinese: 未經檢驗的；未經考驗的
example: Investors hesitated to back an untested technology.

chinese: 不確定的；模糊的；未定的
example: The fossil's age remains indeterminate.
The data sent an unambiguous message: the policy had failed.
The ambiguity of the contract invited competing interpretations.

chinese: 無保留的；完全的；不合格的
example: The play was an unqualified success, praised by every major critic.

chinese: 開脫罪責的；證明無罪的
example: The defense uncovered exculpatory evidence the prosecution had overlooked.
No economist foretold how quickly the market would recover.
Her erudition was evident in footnotes drawing on six languages.
The learned commentary assumes a familiarity with classical texts.
The survey's comprehensiveness made it the standard reference for decades.
An exhaustive search of the archives turned up no trace of the letter.
The wide-ranging interview touched on art, politics, and physics.
The pellucidity of her prose makes difficult ideas seem effortless.

chinese: 無法理解的；難以辨認的
example: Without a glossary the dialect was nearly unintelligible to outsiders.

definition: elegance; an improvement through small changes
example: Each refinement of the model brought its predictions closer to observation.

chinese: 不精密的；粗淺的；單純的
example: The study relied on unsophisticated methods that could not detect subtle effects.

definition: to fail to notice; to ignore
example: Earlier historians overlooked the role of women in the movement.

definition: v. to fail to give attention to; n. failure to care for
chinese: v. 忽視；疏忽；n. 忽略；疏忽
example: The theory neglects factors that later proved decisive.

chinese: 難以察覺的；無法辨別的
example: The difference between the two samples was indiscernible to the naked eye.

definition: not able to be noticed or measured
chinese: 偵測不到的；難以察覺的
example: The contaminant was present at nearly undetectable levels.

definition: the quality of being uniform throughout
example: The town's cultural homogeneity began to fade as newcomers arrived.
Critics lamented the uniformity of suburban architecture.

chinese: 不變通的；死板的；僵硬的
example: An inflexible schedule left no room for unexpected discoveries.
Without new ideas the field began to stagnate.
The government's vacillation on the issue confused allies and rivals alike.

definition: v. to settle or find a solution; to decide firmly; n. firm determination
chinese: v. 解決；決心；n. 決心；堅定
example: The new data resolve a paradox that had puzzled astronomers for decades.
The novel's enduring popularity surprised its own author.

definition: having existed for a long time
chinese: 長期存在的；由來已久的
example: The discovery settled a long-standing dispute among geologists.

definition: v. to deal with; to speak to; n. a formal speech
chinese: v. 處理；應對；致詞；n. 演說；地址
example: The report raises important questions but fails to address them.
Celebrations proved premature when the results were overturned.

definition: serving as a typical example or model
example: Her career is paradigmatic of a generation that moved from labs to startups.
It is paradoxical that the most isolated island had the most diverse dialects.
Witnesses gave contradictory accounts of the night's events.

definition: the ability to think independently and creatively
example: Reviewers praised the originality of a debut that resembled nothing else on the shelf.
The engineers showed great ingenuity in repairing the probe from millions of miles away.
The screenplay relies on every cliché of the detective genre.
The site looked unremarkable until excavation revealed an ancient temple.
His early paintings were competent but unexceptional.
The archive offers unparalleled access to medieval trade records.
An engaging lecturer can make even statistics seem exciting.

definition: openness; the quality of being easily understood
example: Voters demanded greater transparency in campaign financing.

definition: to regard as perfect or better than in reality
example: Nostalgic accounts tend to idealize rural life, ignoring its hardships.

definition: the quality of being hard to solve or control
example: The intractability of the conflict frustrated three generations of diplomats.

definition: to create difficulties that slow progress
example: A lack of reliable data hindered efforts to model the epidemic.
